lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Complex Solutions, Polynomials, and the Binomial Theorem
lessonRef.focus: extending polynomial identities to the complex numbers
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: extending polynomial identities to the complex numbers

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

items.prompt: Factor x² + 9 over the complex numbers.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: A polynomial with real coefficients has degree 5. How many roots does it have in the complex numbers, counted with multiplicity, and what constrains its non-real roots?
choices: exactly 6, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 4, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 3, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 5, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs

items.prompt: In the expansion of (x + y)^7, find the coefficient of the term x^4·y^3.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Complete the statement: the product of two rational expressions …
choices: is always a rational expression, because a common denominator can always be formed
need not be a rational expression, because the denominators may differ
is always a rational expression, because numerators and denominators multiply directly
is always a rational expression, because dividing is multiplying by the reciprocal

items.prompt: Factor x² + 64 completely over the complex numbers.
A polynomial with real coefficients has degree 6. How many roots does it have in the complex numbers, counted with multiplicity, and what constrains its non-real roots?
choices: exactly 3, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 7, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 6, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs
exactly 5, and any non-real roots occur in conjugate pairs

items.prompt: In the expansion of (x + y)^8, find the coefficient of the term x^4·y^4.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.prompt: Complete the statement: the sum of two rational expressions …
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Factor x² + 81 completely over the complex numbers.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
